 the applicant/State.

entities.text:
State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Dharmendra Sethana)
 Indore
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard on the point of admission.

The applicant/State has preferred this peti  section 378(3) of code of criminal procedure, 1973 (for   code'), against the judgment of acquittal dated 11/06/20  Judicial Magistrate First Class, Badwah District Mandles  Nimar) in RCT No.805/2013, whereby the respondent/accuse been acquitted of offence under sections 26(2)(1), 27(2)(c), 27(3)(c), 31(1)(2) read with Sections 51,
52, 59(1), 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class, Badwah District Mandles  Nimar)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is a disputed fact that Food and Safety Officer has taken the sample from the respondent/accused on 14/02/2012, however, the charge-sheet has been filed on 22/08/2013 i.e. after a lapse of one year from the date of occurrence.

Therefore, the trial Court has rightly acquitted the respondent/accused on the ground that the present complaint has not been filed within the prescribed limitation period and there is no perversity found in the judgment passed by the trial Court.
Accordingly, no grounds are available for grant of leave to appeal against the impugned judgment.
Resultantly, M.Cr.C. No.38628/2019 is hereby dismissed being devoid of any merit.
